summary: Oura agreed to buy AI primary-care startup Counsel Health for $625 million cash, the show's defining wearables-to-care deal.
Teladoc launched employer co-pay funding for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs outside the pharmacy benefit, with clients starting January 1, 2027.
Buyers now demand proof of return on investment from AI; vendors face shorter contracts, and 72% of companies still lead with 'AI-powered'.
Medicaid cuts and rising uninsured volumes were flagged as threats to hospital and community health center margins; figures not reported.

items.title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health, AI-native primary care (Oura, private)
lines: Purchase price $625 million cash, subject to purchase-price adjustments; expected to close before end of 2026.
Oura fiscal fourth-quarter revenue $533 million, up 153% year over year; adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization) $87 million, 16% margin.
Oura has more than 6 million members; Counsel was integrated into the Oura app in June 2026.
Deal came weeks after Oura postponed an initial public offering (IPO) of up to $2.2 billion indefinitely, citing IPO-market uncertainty.

items.title: Comprehensive Weight Care employer contribution option for glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs (Teladoc Health)
lines: Employer sets a fixed payment per employee per fill each plan year; employee pays the balance; dollar amounts not reported.
Covers FDA-approved GLP-1s from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk, outside traditional pharmacy benefit design; available now, first clients launch January 1, 2027.
Contribution can be tied to engagement such as food logging and weigh-ins; Lilly Employer Connect is a named channel.
Related: Withings/Calibrate real-world study of nearly 5,000 GLP-1 patients reported about 60% greater weight loss with support program.

items.title: Acquisition of AgileMD clinical decision support and eCART surveillance (Wolters Kluwer)
lines: Up to $100 million: $40 million upfront cash plus up to $60 million performance-based deferred consideration; announced November 13, 2026.
AgileMD projected annual recurring revenue (ARR) $7 million at year-end 2026: 5.7x ARR upfront, 14.3x at full price.
Adds FDA-cleared eCART deterioration surveillance and electronic health record (EHR) pathways to UpToDate Expert AI.
Wolters Kluwer survey at HLTH: only 27% of consumers trust AI to flag drug interactions without a human involved.

items.title: Agentic AI launches: Amazon Health Connect (Amazon Web Services), ChatGPT for Healthcare (OpenAI, private), Suki OS (Suki, private)
lines: Amazon Web Services (AWS) said UC San Diego cut 630 staff phone hours per week using its identity-verification agent capability.
HLTH newsroom: AWS launched a $100 million initiative to expand AI-powered healthcare access globally; timing details not reported.
OpenAI added over 20 plugins and is piloting computer-use agents for prior authorization and discharge planning; figures not reported.
Suki OS agents target prior authorization and coding gaps affecting revenue cycle management (RCM); figures not reported.

items.title: AI spending and return on investment scrutiny (Google Cloud, Ambience Healthcare)
lines: Healthcare AI spending reported at $3.7 billion in 2026, up 250% in one year (figure from an unnamed company, via Vistatec).
Google Cloud: 40% of healthcare organizations see unpredictable costs as a risk to AI projects.
SolComms/HLTH report on 1,600 applicant companies: 72% lead with 'AI-powered'; no surveyed venture capitalists said it raised confidence.
Ambience inpatient AI: Onvida needed 1.5% case mix index (CMI) gain to justify cost and saw 6.5%.

items.title: Consumer wearables as front door: Whoop (private) with Grail, Quest and Novo Nordisk; Apple Health AI Usage Study
lines: Whoop integrated Grail's multi-cancer early detection test and expanded Quest blood testing to non-members; partnered in Novo Nordisk's relaunched NovoCare direct-to-consumer program.
Whoop has raised over $900 million including a $575 million Series G in March 2026, at a $10 billion valuation.
Apple's virtual study with OpenEvidence will observe about 200,000 people using conversational health AI; requires iPhone 15 Pro or newer.
Noom Band wearable launches early 2027 for employer and health-plan clients at no added upfront cost; pricing not reported.

items.title: Clinical AI distribution into provider systems: Doximity at NewYork-Presbyterian; Abridge (private) at community health centers
lines: Doximity expanded its NewYork-Presbyterian deal to put its Ask decision-support and Scribe documentation tools system-wide; contract figures not reported.
Abridge Assistant offered at no cost to 108,000 clinicians at National Association of Community Health Centers (NACHC) members.
NACHC represents 1,534 community health centers serving over 52 million patients; held an Aetna (CVS Health) partnership session.
Medicaid cuts and rising uninsured volumes flagged as margin threats to hospitals and health centers; figures not reported.

expert_minds: AI is commoditized; buyers want validated outcomes, shorter contracts and return-on-investment milestones, and physician groups reject replacement narratives (Chief Healthcare Executive wrap-up).
AI versus affordability: agentic AI and GLP-1 access dominated; the path to affordable access is still a work in progress (Healthcare Dive takeaways).
Prevention moving to continuous, wearable-led care, and women's health becoming a core strategy (Forrester); ARPA-H CMO Rafid Fadul urged faster clinical research.
Buzzwords were agentic harness, AI infrastructure, compounding pharmacy and trust layer; providers and insurers said AI is raising spending (Digital Health Wire; Modern Healthcare).
topics: AI return on investment and procurement
